objective: Define a reproducible, personalized-but-auditable E-S Quest difficulty policy for the ChatGPT System Controller, preserve unscored behavior under uncertainty, and prevent reward farming through task splitting or inflated estimates before the first player-facing Quest v2 quest.

roles_before.artifact: Ron OS and claim-specific live owners determine the real goal, constraints, baseline and completion evidence.
Neon/PostgreSQL system_events remains the sole mutable owner of derived RPG state.
ChatGPT is the sole intended interactive System controller and translates natural language into reviewed System actions.
Quest v2 supports structured objectives, progress, deadlines, visibility/reveal, failure/expiry and one active player quest.
system-quest-reward:v1 maps E-S rank deterministically to XP and coins.
The controller currently forbids guessing difficulty but has no reproducible E-S classification procedure and still contains a stale pre-Quest-v2 section.
Ambiguous quests remain unscored rather than receiving invented XP or coins.
One real action cannot be split or duplicated to farm rewards; one completion basis can reward once.
Persistent System actions require Ron's explicit permission for the exact intended write.
Quest v1 compatibility, legacy LifeUp rollback code and Git history remain preserved.

role_dispositions.destination: The difficulty policy consumes only current evidence from Ron OS, direct Ron evidence and claim-specific live owners; it never promotes System estimates into real-world truth.
Neon/PostgreSQL system_events remains the only mutable RPG-state owner; this candidate performs no production database write.
ChatGPT remains the sole intended controller and applies the versioned rubric before proposing a scored quest.
Existing Quest v2 model, database migrations and lifecycle semantics remain unchanged and covered by the full regression suite.
Difficulty rank continues to feed the existing system-quest-reward:v1 table without changing XP or coin amounts.

system-quest-difficulty:v1 specification plus an executable pure classifier and controller procedure define required inputs, deterministic score bands, adaptive evidence anchors and explainable output.
Missing/low-confidence inputs, unsafe objectives or disputed boundaries return UNSCORED with reason codes and no XP/coin reward.
The policy classifies the smallest independently valuable outcome, rejects artificial split/duplicate/self-inflated scope and records a stable outcome key for controller review.
Candidate work changes repository policy/tests only; any later production quest write still requires exact authorization and read-back.
Quest v1, legacy LifeUp artifacts, prior controller behavior and all history remain recoverable; the change is additive except for replacing the stale pre-Quest-v2 controller block.

capability_probes.assertion: Structured Quest v2 creation, progress, completion, cancellation, failure, expiry, reveal and one-active-player-quest behavior remain unchanged.
Missing evidence, low confidence, unsafe tasks, artificial micro-splits, duplicate outcomes and effort inflated by avoidable delay return UNSCORED rather than a reward rank.
Neon ownership, mutation permission, profile/calibration, PWA projection and retired-LifeUp routing remain intact.
Git history and the manifest preserve the pre-rubric controller procedure and reward mechanics for audit or rollback.

tests.expected: PASS for every E-S boundary, deterministic explanations, adaptive anchors and UNSCORED reason codes.
PASS for missing inputs, low confidence, unsafe tasks, artificial splitting, duplicate outcome keys and inflated waiting/inefficiency.
PASS with Quest v2 live, system-quest-difficulty:v1 referenced, stale pre-Quest-v2 language absent, Neon ownership and exact permission preserved.
PASS for Quest v1/v2, calibration, projection, store and PostgreSQL gates.

tests.command: python tests/architecture_change_guard.py && python tests/architecture_change_guard_selftest.py && python tests/continuity_coverage_guard.py && python tests/lifeup_system_guard.py
tests.expected: PASS with no owner, routing, rollback or legacy capability loss.
